content:
alice: Heads-up — starting ~22:10 UTC we're seeing a concentrated bump in NVIDIA Xid 48 and Xid 31 in eu-west1. Patterns point to small-batch embedder/decoder workloads on A10s. Any recent rollout or kernel/driver changes?
ben: saw the alert too. I checked node reboots for the timeframe — 3 nodes rebooted but they were unrelated maintenance.
carol: no infra-side driver rollouts from our end. Customer-facing config tweak rolled out at 21:50 but it's rate-limiter knob for embeddings, shouldn't touch driver/firmware.
dave: throwing the quick query I used: ```
# PromQL-ish pseudo-query
sum by (gpu_model, xid_code) (increase(gpu_xid_errors_total{region="eu-west1",gpu_model="A10"}[30m]))
```
ben: result: xid48=72, xid31=18 across 6 nodes, mainly tenant cohorts running small batch=1-4.
alice: interesting — xid48 concentrated on one rack (rack-eu-7), xid31 more spread. Could be a flaky card in that rack amplifying backpressure and causing decode retries.
carol: can we get kernel dmesg snippets from the affected nodes? Also check ECC counters: ```
# on node
sudo journalctl -k | grep -i nvidia -A5 -B2
nvidia: Xid (48) GPU fault: reason 0x8b
```
dave: infra-bot: dumped dmesg and ECC counters to /mnt/tmp/xid-2219002468/ — link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/dash/node/xyz (ops only) :lock: 
infra-bot: [automated] Node node-eu-west1-a-17 logged 48 xids=24 in 20m, ECC corrected errors +3, uncorrectable=0.
ben: ECC increased but corrected only. That suggests memory noise rather than hard ECC failures. Could be thermal or PCIe crosstalk. Any temperature spikes?
carol: temps normal in metrics. However PCIe retransmits jumped on the same NIC on those nodes. Could be chassis-level power/PCI riser flake.
alice: I propose: 1) soft-drain the top-2 suspect GPUs on node-eu-west1-a-17, 2) reprovision pods to other racks, 3) schedule hardware swap during low-traffic window if xids persist. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
dave: agree. Use soft-drain first so we preserve tenancy and avoid big rollout. Command example: ```
# cordon + migrate pods (our tooling)
redwoodctl node cordon node-eu-west1-a-17
redwoodctl gpu set-drain node-eu-west1-a-17 gpu-3 --soft
```
ben: I'll kick off soft-drain on gpu-3 and gpu-5 now. Notifying affected tenants (embedding heavy) via ops roster.
ops-roster: @channel Notified 3 tenants with top load on those GPUs — they'll see temporary tail-latency bump as we migrate.
carol: after drain starts, monitor Xid rates. If they drop to baseline, that's strong signal card-level issue. If they continue on other cards, look at workload pattern/driver interaction.
alice: also consider reproducer: spin up a small-batch embedder replica with identical model/seq on a healthy A10 and run high-concurrency loop to see if we can trigger Xid locally. Keep it in a separate tenant sandbox.
dave: started reproducer on node-eu-west1-b-04 with same model/config. Will post logs in 30m.
infra-bot: [automated] Drift rule: if node sees >50 xid48 in 15m after drain, auto-schedule physical replacement.
ben: drain finished. Early signal: xid48 dropped 80% on node-eu-west1-a-17, spikes moved to other racks but at lower amplitude.
alice: good — treat gpu-3 as candidate flaky. I'll create hardware ticket for on-site swap (part: PCI riser + card reseat) and set stress window in 6 hours. Filing now.
carol: add note to telemetry: correlate op-type (decode vs embed) and batch-size — looks like very small batch+short seq decode path triggers something in A10 decode kernel under noisy PCI.
dave: logging follow-up: attach pcie error counts & nvlink stats to ticket. Also include the reproducer run result once complete.
alice: thanks all. We'll watch for recurrence over 24h and escalate to supplier RMA if phys swap doesn't eliminate. Closing this thread once hardware ticket created. :white_check_mark:
